  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most

answer.rationale: The two measured declines this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and two independent inherited records (memory_31 SMB signup simplification, memory_86 shortened onboarding) point at the same lever with durable rather than one-window effects. That convergence is why simplify_onboarding is my intended action over the more tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing. I want memory_73 verified precisely because it is the memory most likely to pull the org toward promotional_pricing right now: a 31% conversion and 18% revenue lift is exactly the shape of result that decays after the 12-week window it was observed in, and the record itself notes the support model was unchanged, so we never learned whether discount-acquired low-touch accounts are retainable or qualified. If the archived record shows the lift was measured on conversions rather than on retained revenue, promo is a margin trade against the primary objective, not a fix. I want memory_86 verified because it is the load-bearing evidence for my own choice and I should test it at least as hard: I need to know whether the completion lift translated into retained, paying accounts or only into faster funnel movement, and whether the current -4% is the same failure mode the original test addressed or a new one (competitor-driven mix shift toward price-sensitive signups who would churn anyway). Downstream risk I am flagging rather than assuming away: memory_44 says enterprise converts better through sales-assisted flows, so cutting required signup fields can strip the qualification signal that routes prospects to demo-request. Volume of activations could rise while qualified pipeline falls, which would look like success on the proximate metric and a loss on the actual objective. I am therefore scoping the experiment to the SMB self-serve segment, leaving the enterprise path untouched, and instrumenting on retained qualified revenue and downstream pipeline quality, not completion rate alone. Uncertainty I am not resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, none state effect durability beyond their observation windows, and none were measured under competitive price pressure, so prior effect sizes should be treated as upper bounds. If verification undercuts memory_86, referral_incentive (memory_57, which explicitly reports no retention harm) is my fallback rather than promotional_pricing.
